title: Beyond the Hype: Level up your AI game as a Tester
description:
We've been here before. Manual testing gave way to automation, and the Testers who adapted thrived. AI is that moment again, and it's moving faster.
If you've ever thought "there's so much going on with AI right now, I don't know where to start" or "I'm using it a bit but what's actually next?", this session is built for you.

This is for Testers/ QA/ QE engineers and Leads at every stage of the journey, whether you just got sign-off to try an AI tool or you're already using one to write your e2e tests. We'll make the case for why QE judgment matters more than ever in a world of non-deterministic software, and walk through a practical five-level framework for getting AI working in your day-to-day.
Then we roll up our sleeves.

**Format**
A short talk talk followed by a hands-on workshop where we'll brainstorm real use cases together. The workshop is structured so you can contribute at whatever level you're at. If you've never used an AI tool for testing, you'll leave with your first concrete use case. If you're already automating with AI, we'll push into the harder problems.

**What you'll take away**
A clear next step to "where do I actually start?" You'll leave with a working mental model for what good AI-assisted testing looks like at each stage of maturity, and at least one thing you can try the next day.

title: Auckland Voices: Tracing the history of the New Zealand accent
location: Whare Wānanga, Central Library, Level 2, 44 Lorne Street, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Where did the New Zealand accent come from and why does it sound the way it does today?
Auckland Voices is a project exploring over 100 years of speech in Auckland to try answer that question. Surprisingly, Auckland, NZ’s largest urban centre, has been notably underrepresented in research on the origins of our accent. Past work has been largely South Island and rurally focused, however newly rediscovered historical writings suggest the NZ accent may have developed fastest in the North Island, particularly in Auckland. 
In this talk, we’ll share how we’re using oral history recordings from the Auckland Council Libraries archives to investigate these historical claims and discuss what these valuable resources can teach us about the emergence of our unique accent.
Dr Brooke Ross is a Postdoctoral Fellow in the Faculty of Engineering and Design at the University of Auckland. With a background in Linguistics and Speech Science, her interdisciplinary research uses speech technology to understand how and why the New Zealand accent is changing over time.
This project team also includes:

Professor Catherine Watson (Faculty of Engineering and Design, UoA)
Associate Professor Elaine Ballard (Faculty of Science, UoA)
Miriam Meyerhoff (All Souls College, University of Oxford).

Tāmaki untold: conversations celebrating the taonga, stories and creativity of Auckland. A curated monthly talk series held in the Whare Wānanga hosted by Research and Heritage Services, Auckland Libraries.
